title: Use low-specificity panel bases for consumer overrides
context: The previous panel fix used duplicated consumer class selectors to outrank a shared PanelCard base. Replace that workaround with an intentionally low-specificity base rule, restore ordinary consumer selectors, and protect the linked case-study surface radius from the same cross-module ordering issue.

tasks.title: Make reusable panel bases low-specificity and cover case cards
acceptance_criteria: PanelCard uses a low-specificity base selector so normal consumer class selectors override its shared border, radius, background, backdrop, and shadow declarations regardless of stylesheet order
Homepage skillCard and availabilityCard use ordinary single-class selectors and retain their intended direct-load and client-navigation styles
LinkedPanelCard case-study surfaces retain the compact desktop radius after a shared base rule arrives last
The Playwright regression verifies all three skill-card tone borders, the availability card, and both case-study surfaces before and after the simulated late base rule
